The separate (b) speech family is not used, and forms with kō auxiliaries are excluded. The paired elicitation gloss is retained even where this individual source record contains only the bare/imperative or inflected verb; no absent clause is reconstructed. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1524 gives Tamil kiṭa lie/rest with kiṭant- past, Malayalam kiṭakka and Kannada keḍe/kaḍe fall. Survey kiḍa/kɛḍa/kaḍa and kiḍand-/kiḍann- participial forms retain the recumbency stem; causative-looking or auxiliary-extended responses are not silently merged. Paired prompt wording and each source form remain unchanged; longer responses with an additional verb are excluded. The existing reconstructed parent *kōḍ- (?) is explicitly uncertain; that uncertainty is retained, and the questioned Malto comparison is not used as evidence. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
